name: Addition Quest
description: Fifty-two ways to add, from counting two groups to the strategies that make counting unnecessary.
author: Koda Math Lab
tagline: Put groups together, then learn the shortcuts.

features.name: Spoken voice
features.description: Reads the question aloud when it opens, counts along as a child taps, and speaks every hint. Turn off for a silent lesson.

features.name: Sound chimes
features.description: Pop and success chimes as objects are touched.

features.name: Haptic vibration
features.description: A vibration pulse on each tap and each completed group.

features.name: 1-to-1 badges
features.description: Numbers each touched object, so nothing is counted twice.

features.name: Running total
features.description: Shows the count so far beside the groups, as it grows.

features.name: Step framing tags
features.description: Labels each step — warm-up, guided challenge, final milestone — beside the step counter.

settingsSchema.label: Warm-up tag
settingsSchema.help: Wording for step 1. Leave blank to use the default.

settingsSchema.label: Activity tag
settingsSchema.help: Wording for even-numbered steps. Leave blank to use the default.

settingsSchema.label: Guided tag
settingsSchema.help: Wording for odd-numbered steps. Leave blank to use the default.

settingsSchema.help: Wording for the last step. Leave blank to use the default.

settingsSchema.label: Speech rate
settingsSchema.help: How fast the counter and the hints are spoken.

lessons.title: Count Them All
lessons.concept: Joining Two Groups by Counting Every One

play.shortDesc: Touch every object in both groups to find how many there are altogether
play.targetObjective: Count both groups, one object at a time.
stepByStep: Look at the two groups.
Touch every object in the first group, then keep going into the second.
The last number you say is how many there are altogether.
play.kidTip: Do not start again at the second group. Keep counting on.
play.audioPrompt: Count them all! Touch every one in both groups to find how many altogether.

prompts.default: Count them all. How many altogether?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Counting all is where addition starts: a child who counts both groups from one is not behind, they are building the idea the shortcuts will later replace.

lessons.title: Put Them Together

play.shortDesc: Slide two groups into one pile, then count the pile
play.targetObjective: Put the two groups together, then count them.
stepByStep: Look at the two groups on their own.
Tap Put them together to make one pile.
Touch every object in the pile to count it.
play.kidTip: Adding means putting groups together. Then you count once.
play.audioPrompt: Put the two groups together, then count how many you have.

prompts.default: Put the groups together, then count them all.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Seeing two sets physically become one is what makes the plus sign mean something later.

lessons.title: Count On
lessons.concept: Starting from a Number Instead of from One

play.shortDesc: Hold the first number in your head and count on for the rest
play.targetObjective: Say the first number, then count on.
stepByStep: The first group is closed. Its number is written on the lid.
Say that number to yourself — you do not need to count it.
Touch the objects in the second group, counting on from there.
play.kidTip: The closed box is already counted. Start from its number.
play.audioPrompt: Count on! The first group is already counted, so start from its number.

prompts.default: Start at {a} and count on.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Counting on is the first real strategy: it treats the first number as a quantity rather than as something to be re-counted.

lessons.title: Start with the Bigger Number
lessons.concept: Counting On from the Larger Addend

play.shortDesc: Choose the bigger number to start from, so there is less to count
play.targetObjective: Start from the bigger number. It is less work.
stepByStep: Look at both numbers before you start.
Tap the bigger one to start from it.
Count on the smaller group — there are fewer to touch.
play.kidTip: You can add in any order, so start from the bigger number.
play.audioPrompt: Start with the bigger number! Then you have fewer to count on.

prompts.default: Start with the bigger number, then count on.

lessons.pedagogyTip: 3 + 8 and 8 + 3 give the same total, and one of them takes three counts instead of eight. That choice is the lesson.

lessons.title: Adding Zero

play.shortDesc: See that an empty group leaves the total exactly as it was
play.targetObjective: Adding zero leaves the number alone.
stepByStep: One group has objects. The other group is empty.
Nothing is being added, so nothing changes.
Choose the number you started with.
play.kidTip: Zero means none. The number stays the same.
play.audioPrompt: Adding zero! One group is empty, so what happens to the total?

prompts.default: What is {a} plus {b}?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Children who have only ever counted find zero genuinely strange — an empty group is still a group, and it still gets added.

lessons.title: Adding One
lessons.concept: One More Is the Next Number

play.shortDesc: Recognise that adding one just moves you to the next counting number
play.targetObjective: One more is the very next number.
stepByStep: Look at how many are in the big group.
One more is being added.
Say the next counting number — that is the answer.
play.kidTip: Adding one is just saying the next number.
play.audioPrompt: Adding one! One more is the next number you say when you count.

prompts.default: What is {a} plus {b}?

lessons.pedagogyTip: This is where the counting sequence stops being a song and starts being arithmetic: the number after seven *is* seven and one more.

lessons.title: Use Your Fingers
lessons.concept: Modelling Both Addends on Two Hands

play.shortDesc: Put one number on each hand, then count all the raised fingers
play.targetObjective: One number on each hand, then count them all.
stepByStep: Raise the first number of fingers on the left hand.
Raise the second number on the right hand.
Count every raised finger to find the total.
play.kidTip: One number on each hand. Then count every finger that is up.
play.audioPrompt: Use your fingers! Put one number on each hand, then count them all.

prompts.default: Show {a} on one hand and {b} on the other. How many fingers altogether?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Fingers are a manipulative a child always has. Discouraging them removes the model before the fact is known, which is what produces guessing.

lessons.title: Five Frame
lessons.concept: Adding Inside a Frame of Five

play.shortDesc: Add counters to a row of five and read the total without counting from one
play.targetObjective: Fill the frame, then read how many.
stepByStep: Some counters are already in the frame.
Tap empty spaces to add the rest.
The frame shows the total — you do not have to start again at one.
play.kidTip: The frame is already counted. Count on from the number in it.
play.audioPrompt: Five frame! Add counters to the row, then say how many there are.

prompts.default: Fill in {b} more. How many are there altogether?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Five is the first benchmark. A child who sees four as 'one less than five' has stopped counting one at a time.

lessons.title: Ten Frame
lessons.concept: Adding Inside a Frame of Ten

play.shortDesc: Add counters to two rows of five and read the total at a glance
play.targetObjective: Fill the frame, then read how many.
stepByStep: The top row holds five. The bottom row holds five more.
Tap empty spaces to add counters.
A full row of five helps you see the total without counting.
play.kidTip: A full top row is five. Count on from there.
play.audioPrompt: Ten frame! Add counters to the frame, then say how many altogether.

prompts.default: Fill in {b} more. How many are there altogether?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Two rows of five is what makes ten readable at a glance, and it is the structure every make-ten strategy later leans on.

lessons.title: Number Bonds

play.shortDesc: Read a bond diagram and give the whole that its two parts make
play.targetObjective: Two parts underneath make the whole on top.
stepByStep: The two boxes at the bottom are the parts.
The box at the top is the whole they make together.
Tap the empty box and type the whole.
play.kidTip: The two parts underneath make the whole on top.
play.audioPrompt: Number bonds! The two parts at the bottom make the whole at the top.

prompts.default: What do {a} and {b} make altogether?

lessons.pedagogyTip: A bond is the picture behind every later decomposition — breaking an addend, finding a missing part, and fact families are all this diagram with a different box blank.

name: Counting Quest
description: One-to-one correspondence, subitizing and quantity comparison.
author: Koda Math Lab
tagline: Count, compare and see small amounts at a glance.

features.name: Haptic vibration

lessons.title: Count the Row

play.shortDesc: Tap objects in a straight line from left to right to find the total count
play.targetObjective: Touch each one. The last number tells how many.
stepByStep: Touch each item once from left to right in order.
Listen as the numbers count up: 1, 2, 3...
The last number tells you how many there are in all.
play.kidTip: Say one number for each one you touch.
play.audioPrompt: Count in a row! Touch each item in order to find the total.

prompts.default: Touch each {item}. Count as you go!

lessons.pedagogyTip: The last number named represents the whole group (cardinality). Keep your finger taps in sync with the numbers!

lessons.title: Count Them All

play.shortDesc: Touch all scattered objects across the screen without skipping or double-counting
play.targetObjective: Touch every one. Do not miss any!
stepByStep: Look across the screen from top to bottom.
Tap each uncounted item once to give it a number tag.
Make sure every item is counted without skipping any.
play.kidTip: Go in order so you do not miss any.
play.audioPrompt: Count scattered objects! Tap each one once until all are counted.

prompts.default: Touch every {item}. Do not miss any!

lessons.pedagogyTip: Scanning in an orderly way (like top to bottom) helps count scattered items accurately.

lessons.title: Which Group Has More?

play.shortDesc: See that spreading items out or grouping them does not change the total count
play.targetObjective: Count both groups. Which one has more?
stepByStep: Look at Group A (clustered) and Group B (spread out in a line).
Count the items in both groups.
Confirm that both groups have the exact same count.
play.kidTip: Spreading things out does not make more!
play.audioPrompt: Compare both groups! Do they have the same number of items?

prompts.same: Count both groups. Do they have the same?
prompts.different: Count both groups. Which one has more?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Spreading items out might make a group look bigger, but the actual count stays exactly the same!

lessons.title: Dice Dots

play.shortDesc: Recognize dice dot patterns in a quick flash without counting one by one
play.targetObjective: Look fast! How many dots did you see?
stepByStep: Look at the center when the dots flash.
Recognize the dot pattern right away.
Tap the matching number on the keypad.
play.kidTip: Try to see the pattern without counting.
play.audioPrompt: Quick Dice Flash! Look at the dots and tap the number right away.

prompts.default: Look fast! How many did you see?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Recognizing dot patterns right away (subitizing) builds strong mental number pictures.

lessons.title: How Many Dots?

play.shortDesc: Recognize scattered dot amounts in a fast flash without one-by-one counting
play.targetObjective: Look fast! How many dots?
stepByStep: Look at the dot group as a whole.
Feel how many dots are there without counting each one.
Tap your answer on the number pad.
play.kidTip: Look for small groups inside the big group.
play.audioPrompt: Quick Dot Groups! Look quickly and tap the count.

prompts.default: Look fast! How many did you see?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Seeing dot groups at a glance helps you think of numbers as solid quantities.

lessons.title: Two Colours, One Total

play.shortDesc: See two colored groups in a flash and combine them together (e.g. 3 + 4 = 7)
play.targetObjective: Two colours. How many all together?
stepByStep: Look at the two different color groups in the flash.
Notice how many in Color 1 and how many in Color 2.
Add both parts together in your head to find the total.
play.kidTip: Count one colour, then keep going with the other.
play.audioPrompt: Combine Two Colors! Add both color groups in your head and tap the total.

prompts.default: Look fast! How many did you see?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Seeing numbers as two parts (like 5 is 3 and 2) makes mental addition fast and easy.

lessons.title: Five and Some More

play.shortDesc: Fill the top 5 first as your anchor, then add more on the bottom row
play.targetObjective: Fill the top row first. Then add more.
stepByStep: Look at your target number (like 7 or 8).
Fill all 5 cells in the top row first.
Add the remaining dots in the bottom row (7 is 5 + 2).
Tap Launch when your ten-frame is complete.
play.kidTip: Fill the top row to 5 first. That makes it easy!
play.audioPrompt: Ten-Frame! Fill 5 on top first, then add the rest on the bottom.

prompts.default: Make {target} dots. Fill the top row first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Seeing numbers using 5 (like 8 is 5 + 3) makes mental math simple.

lessons.title: Friends of Ten

play.shortDesc: Find how many empty spaces are needed to make a full ten-frame of 10
play.targetObjective: How many more to make 10?
stepByStep: Look at the dots already placed in the ten-frame.
Count the empty spaces needed to reach 10.
Select the missing number that makes 10 with the dots.
play.kidTip: Count the empty boxes. That is how many more.
play.audioPrompt: Making 10! Find how many more dots are needed to reach 10.

prompts.default: You have {have}. How many more to make 10?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Pairs that make 10 (like 7 + 3 and 6 + 4) are key building blocks for all math!

lessons.title: Teen Numbers

play.shortDesc: Build numbers from 11 to 19 using 1 full ten-frame plus extra ones
play.targetObjective: Fill one frame to make 10. Then add more.
stepByStep: Notice the first ten-frame is full with 10.
Add dots to the second frame for the ones digit.
See that 10 and ones make the teen number (10 + 4 = 14).
play.kidTip: One full frame is 10. Then count the extra ones.
play.audioPrompt: Teen Numbers! Combine one full ten with extra ones.

prompts.default: Make {target}. Fill one frame with 10, then add more.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Every teen number is simply 'one ten and some ones'. Double ten-frames show this clearly.

lessons.title: Hop by 2s and 5s

play.shortDesc: Hop along the path by equal steps of 2 or 5 to reach the goal
play.targetObjective: Hop the same size steps. Count as you go!
stepByStep: Check the step size (+2 or +5) on the path.
Tap Hop to jump forward by equal amounts.
Chant the numbers aloud as you hop all the way to the goal.
play.kidTip: Say the numbers out loud as you hop.
play.audioPrompt: Skip Counting! Hop forward by equal steps of 2 or 5.

prompts.default: Hop by {step} to get to {target}!

lessons.pedagogyTip: Skip counting creates equal steps in your mind and prepares you for multiplication.

lessons.title: Big Hops of Ten
lessons.concept: Decade Jumps and Patterns up to 100

play.shortDesc: Take big leaps of 10 to move smoothly along the path up to 100
play.targetObjective: Big hops of 10! Count up to 100.
stepByStep: Check the starting number and the +10 step size.
Notice how the tens digit increases with every hop.
Hop all the way across the path to the target.
play.kidTip: Every hop adds 10. Listen to the pattern!
play.audioPrompt: Count by 10s! Take leaps of 10 to move across the path.

prompts.default: Hop by 10 all the way to {target}!

lessons.pedagogyTip: Counting by 10s (10, 20, 30... 100) helps you navigate place value with ease.

lessons.title: Find the Missing Number

play.shortDesc: Discover the step rule in the sequence and fill in the missing number
play.targetObjective: Which number is missing?
stepByStep: Check the difference between the numbers shown.
See if the numbers are counting up (+) or down (-).
Choose the correct missing number to complete the line.
play.kidTip: Look at how much it grows each hop.
play.audioPrompt: Missing Number! Look at the pattern and pick the missing step.

prompts.default: Which number is missing?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Finding missing numbers in a line helps you understand how all numbers connect.

lessons.title: Make a Ten

play.shortDesc: Gather 10 loose single blocks and group them into 1 solid Ten-Rod
play.targetObjective: Put 10 ones together. They make 1 ten!
stepByStep: Look at your loose single blocks.
Gather 10 single blocks together.
Group 10 ones into 1 solid Ten-Rod.
play.kidTip: 10 ones make 1 ten. Put them together!
play.audioPrompt: Make a Ten! Gather 10 single blocks and group them into 1 Ten-Rod.

prompts.bundle: You made {target}! Now put 10 ones together to make a ten.

lessons.pedagogyTip: 10 loose ones can be grouped together and treated as 1 single 'Ten'.

lessons.title: Make a Hundred
lessons.concept: Place Value: Hundreds, Tens, and Ones

play.shortDesc: Group 10 Ten-Rods into 1 Hundred-Flat and see numbers in expanded form
play.targetObjective: Put 10 tens together. They make 100!
stepByStep: Group Ten-Rods into a 100-Flat whenever you have 10 tens.
Watch the place value counter show Hundreds, Tens, and Ones.
See that the total amount stays the same when grouped.
play.kidTip: 10 tens make 1 hundred. Put them together!
play.audioPrompt: Make a Hundred! Group 10 Ten-Rods into 100-Flats.

prompts.bundle: You reached {target}! Now fuse 10 Tens into a Hundred to bundle your numbers. Click "Fuse 10 Tens" below!
prompts.ready: Excellent! You built {target} in the most bundled way. Click "Check" to complete this step!

lessons.pedagogyTip: Expanded form (100 + 30 + 5 = 135) connects physical blocks directly to written numbers.

lessons.title: Build Big Numbers
lessons.concept: Building Numbers up to 100 and Beyond

play.shortDesc: Build any given number using hundreds, tens, and single ones blocks
play.targetObjective: Build the number with the blocks.
stepByStep: Look at your target number.
Use blocks (+), group (⚡), and break apart (🔄) to make the exact amount.
Tap Check Number to test your build.
play.kidTip: Use big blocks first, then the small ones.
play.audioPrompt: Place Value Master! Build the target number using hundreds, tens, and ones.

prompts.add: Build {target}: You have {have} blocks. Add {diff} more using the (+) buttons!
prompts.remove: Build {target}: You have {have} blocks. Remove {diff} using the (-) buttons!
prompts.bundleOnes: You reached {target}! Make a Ten into a Ten to bundle your numbers. Click "Make a Ten" below!
prompts.bundle: You reached {target}! Fuse 10 Tens into a Hundred to bundle your numbers. Click "Fuse 10 Tens" below!
prompts.ready: Congratulations! You built exactly {target} in standard bundled form. Click "Check" to finish!

lessons.pedagogyTip: Breaking a Ten into 10 Ones is the physical secret behind subtraction regrouping.
